The persistence of the different component stocks of the 'Muguga cocktail' in vaccinated cattle is crucial for maintaining long-term immunity against East Coast fever. Studies in Uganda have investigated the persistence of these vaccine stocks to ensure that the vaccine continues to provide protection over time. The findings indicate that all three stocks—Muguga, Kiambu 5, and Serengeti-transformed—can persist in vaccinated cattle, although their levels may vary. This persistence is important because it ensures that the immune system remains primed against multiple strains of , thereby providing broader protection. However, the duration and stability of this persistence can be influenced by several factors, including the initial dose of the vaccine, the health status of the cattle, and environmental conditions.
